Assertions.Description: Disabling through Settings removes the Awake process and tray icon and disables behavior controls.
Enabling restores the process, tray icon and retained active mode.
Both enablement transitions leave other modules' enabled values unchanged.
Passive mode remains resident, disables screen configuration and releases Awake system/display requests.
Indefinite mode with screen off requests system wakefulness without a display request.
Keep screen on adds the display request; switching it off removes only that request.
Mode/display transitions do not modify the active Windows power plan or its settings.
With an independent idle/display observer and controlled timeouts, the active mode prevents actual idle sleep and keep-screen-on prevents display timeout.
Committed 1-hour/2-minute fields persist, activate timed state and hide expiration controls.
A full 0-hour/1-minute interval expires to passive in Settings and runtime without terminating integrated Awake.
Toggling display during the one-minute countdown changes its request without restarting the original deadline.
Selecting passive cancels a running interval and releases requests before its deadline.
Date and time picker commits persist a future deadline and duration controls are hidden.
Future expiration activates system wakefulness and respects the selected display setting.
Actual expiration returns integrated Settings/runtime to passive while Awake remains resident.
Left click opens the real integrated menu with mode/display controls, disabled expiration information and no standalone Exit.
Right click independently opens the same integrated menu and applicable controls.
Tray indefinite and passive selections synchronize Settings, persisted state, tray status and runtime requests.
Tray Keep screen on toggles synchronize Settings, persistence, tray status and display requests.
With default tray times, independently select 30 minutes, 1 hour and 2 hours and observe each corresponding persisted duration and active runtime state.
With a preconfigured two-or-more-entry customTrayTimes fixture, first and last labels dispatch their own configured duration; preserve labels, values and order.
On an authorized disposable post-OS-update/session-start fixture, the enabled icon appears and is removed on disable.
Each of --help, -h and -? visibly displays documented options in an owned parent terminal, returns zero and creates no resident instance.
--time-limit -1 visibly reports an invalid interval, exits nonzero and leaves no new process/power request.
--pid not-a-pid visibly reports an invalid PID, exits nonzero and leaves no new process/power request.
--expire-at not-a-date visibly reports an invalid deadline, exits nonzero and leaves no new process/power request.
With integrated Awake disabled, no-argument standalone mode requests system-only wakefulness and the owned session's user-facing close releases it.
Separate --display-on and --display-on false standalone runs request the corresponding display state and release requests on user-facing close.
-t 20 -d holds system/display requests for the requested interval, then actually exits and releases them.
An approximately 30-second --expire-at deadline takes precedence over --time-limit 300 and actually exits/releases requests at that deadline.
Standalone arguments leave integrated preferences and active Windows power-plan settings unchanged.
--pid keeps Awake active while an owned target lives and Awake exits/releases requests after that target exits naturally.
--use-parent-pid keeps Awake active while its owned parent lives and Awake exits/releases requests after the parent exits.
With integrated instance disabled, --use-pt-config overrides conflicting --display-on and --time-limit 1 arguments with saved mode/display preferences.
Settings UI mode/display edits reach the same configuration-bound CLI process, which remains resident on passive; no JSON setup bypass.
On a recoverable dedicated session and build containing the lock change, startup while locked suppresses display but retains active system request.
Actual workstation lock removes the configured display request but retains active system request.
Actual unlock restores the configured active system/display requests.
On a dedicated recoverable fixture, real sleep/resume reapplies active requests and Settings remains functional.
On suitable hardware, both actual AC-to-battery and battery-to-AC transitions reapply active requests.
With authorized failure instrumentation, SetThreadExecutionState failure logs an error and returns to passive/tray fallback.
The shipped PowerToys extension opens Awake Settings through its Settings command.
When enabled, independently execute indefinite, 30-minute, 1-hour, 2-hour and Turn off commands; refreshed status, Settings and runtime agree.
When Awake is disabled, Settings entry remains while active-mode commands are absent.
Check for updates with Awake enabled and separately disabled preserves that choice and every other module enabled value; no update installation.
On an authorized disposable missing-module/shutdown fixture, a disabled Awake choice survives unavailable-module persistence and shutdown/restart.
With authorized disabled-policy fixture, Settings and standalone activation are blocked while visible --help succeeds; restore the original policy.
With consented diagnostic viewing available, fresh mode-change events correlate with the run's actual mode transitions.
With consented diagnostic viewing available, fresh Awake_CLICommand events distinguish successful and failed CLI actions in this run.
Retain the complete baseline's open-ended feature-exploration requirement; its missing feature list and acceptance oracle require review, not inferred PASS.
